cells.tense: You know already what is fair to do here, and the practice asks nothing more than that.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: The next finished stretch of practice, before starting anything new, sit with what it left: the steadier hand, the hour, the ease. Add it up once. Then close the notebook and let the next round start clean.
cells.sheetLine: The practice is fair to you. Collect what it grew.
cells.core:
You sit down when you said you would. You carry what is yours and not more than that, and the practice keeps its small light on attention rather than on second-guessing. Nothing in it is waiting to be excused. When a round is done it stays done, and the finished work sits there beside you.

The part worth tending is the taking-in. The practice has grown something real — a habit that now holds, a strength you built — and you are entitled to it. Name one finished piece and what it gave you. Once is enough; stop circling back to confirm it happened. What was gathered belongs in your hands, and the hands can rest after they have put it down.

cells.tense: You are running the fairness forward, and the practice will be judged before it is even done.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Once this week, give a real piece of help — small, concrete — and see it through to the end. Hand it over complete. Then let the week go on without checking whether it was enough.
cells.sheetLine: You look at the practice like a debt. Help once, then stop.
cells.core:
You run the weighing forward: whether enough was done, whether what you built will hold, whether the work will be measured fairly once it is seen. It comes down on the practice as something owed before it is earned. That strain has something worth understanding in it, and it says nothing about your history — only that felt fairness is working hard at the front end.

The way back spends that strength outside your own account, once, on someone, and stops. Give a real piece of help this week — small, concrete, finished. Carry it through and hand it over complete. Then stop. What is unfinished stays unfinished. Help that lands somewhere else does not have to be repaid, and the account you were running closes by itself when you leave it.

cells.tense: You were being fair about the practice, and you are still standing at its door after the work is done.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: Tell one person, once, the way you found through a hard part of this work — what helped you, plainly. Say it and then step back. What they do with it belongs to them.
cells.sheetLine: You were fair about the practice. Now show someone the way.
cells.core:
You were being fair, and the fair thing looked like holding back. So the practice is a threshold you keep checking rather than a place you have entered — you keep asking what you owe it, and you do not arrive. It felt like honesty then. It is not the truth now.

What is missing is the passage, not a verdict: not more hours, not stronger effort, but the route another person can take because you already found it. Show one person the way you found through something hard here, plainly, once. The route you found, once it is spoken to someone else, carries you along it too.

cells.tense: Something in the practice knows what is fair, and you are calling that the method's own standard.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: Notice, over the next few days, one habitual move in your practice — a pace, a rule, a way of holding a hard part. Ask where it came from. Mark what you chose and what you took on from someone else.
cells.sheetLine: You think the practice has rules. Some of them are yours.
cells.core:
The practice runs on a sense of what is right, and you believe it is the method speaking. A pace, a rule, a way of holding a hard part — the story you tell is that the work requires it. The work requires some of it. You are doing the rest, and from inside the practice the two are indistinguishable.

What is yours here is the say-so. Name one habitual piece of this practice, once, as something you chose — not as the standard, not as what the work demands of you. You do not have to defend it or explain it. It is simply yours, and with a name on it you can keep it or drop it. What is authored can be revised, and that is the same as being real.
